extracted.intended_audience: science journalists and public information officers (PIOs)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing and issuing science press releases and public-facing research communications that accurately represent studies and meet best-practice PR standards. Emphasizes accuracy, sourcing, framing, multimedia, embargo/communication practices, and avoidance of common hype/anti-patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match study conclusions exactly
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the press release conclusions mirror the paper's conclusions without amplification or added claims; avoid enthusiasm that goes beyond the paper (see anti-patterns such as 'first'/'breakthrough').

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology summary clear
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a concise, understandable summary of methods so readers and reporters can judge study design and limitations; include a methodology document and share full paper PDF when available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect sizes given fully (relative + absolute)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report both relative and absolute effect sizes to prevent misleading impressions about magnitude and clinical/public health importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations explicitly stated
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List study limitations up front so readers understand weaknesses, generalizability issues, and the need for replication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding sources disclosed
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify funders to provide transparency about possible influences on study design, interpretation, or reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of interest noted
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declare any author or institutional conflicts of interest so readers can assess potential bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal investigator interviewed
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the lead researcher(s) as a source to ensure accurate representation of the study, interpretation, and limitations; confirm author availability for media inquiries.

rubrics_metrics.name: External expert quote when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include independent expert perspectives to contextualize findings; provide external expert contacts and consult external reviewers when necessary (e.g., statistical reviewer).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patient/affected community voice when relevant
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When research affects a patient group or community, include affected voices to reflect real-world relevance and implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple perspectives on controversial topics
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For contested findings, present diverse viewpoints rather than single-source claims to avoid misleading or one-sided narratives.

rubrics_metrics.name: No single-source claims on contested findings
rubrics_metrics.description: No single-source claims on contested findings
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid asserting conclusions based on a single source when the topic is contested; seek corroboration and external comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish preclinical from clinical
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state whether the research is preclinical (e.g., lab, bench) or clinical to avoid overstating relevance to human health.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish animal from human studies
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make clear when results are from animal models versus human subjects; avoid implying human applicability for animal findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish association from causation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid causal language for correlational studies; clearly label observational findings as associations and explain limits on causal inference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge replication needs
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note whether findings have been replicated, and explicitly state when additional studies are required to confirm results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Note generalizability limits
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the populations/settings to which results do or do not apply; caution against overgeneralizing beyond the study sample.

rubrics_metrics.name: Researcher photos with consent
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use photographs only with documented consent; ensure appropriate credits and permissions are included in captions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology visualizations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear visualizations of methods (e.g., study flowcharts) to help nontechnical audiences understand design and limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data charts properly labeled
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label axes, units, sample sizes and statistical measures clearly to avoid misinterpretation of figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Captions with proper credits
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include full caption information and source/credit lines for images, figures, and multimedia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alt text for accessibility
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide descriptive alt text for images and data visualizations so content is accessible to people using assistive technologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors review before release
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have study authors review the press release to confirm accuracy and that conclusions match the paper; coordinate author availability for media.

rubrics_metrics.name: External experts consulted
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek outside expert review to contextualize findings and identify overstatement, methodological issues, or missing caveats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical reviewer engaged
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a statistical reviewer to check analyses and effect-size reporting to avoid misinterpretation or statistical errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear separation of facts from speculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear separation of facts from speculation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly mark speculative statements (e.g., implications, hypotheses, future directions) separate from reported results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Future research clearly distinguished from current findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Future research clearly distinguished from current findings
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate suggestions for future work from the study's demonstrated results to prevent conflation of what was shown versus what might be done next.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid press release more enthusiastic than paper
rubrics_metrics.description: Press release more enthusiastic than paper
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern — don't hype or use more sensational language in the release than in the source paper; match tone to evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid 'first' or 'breakthrough' claims without verification
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern — don't label findings as 'first' or 'breakthrough' unless thoroughly verified by literature review and expert corroboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid hyping subgroup findings as primary
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern — avoid presenting subgroup or exploratory results as if they were primary, adequately powered, or definitive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid causal language for correlations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern — do not use causal phrasing when data only support associations; explicitly state observational nature where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid framing single-arm studies as definitive
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern — single-arm or uncontrolled studies should not be presented as proving efficacy or causation; state design limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid portraying surrogate endpoints as clinical outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Surrogate endpoints framed as clinical outcomes
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern — clarify when outcomes are surrogate markers rather than direct clinical endpoints and avoid implying direct clinical benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embargo respected universally
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to embargo agreements consistently; respect agreed-upon release times to preserve fair access for media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materials sent 48-72 hours before lift
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide journalists with materials (under embargo) 48–72 hours before the embargo lifts to allow thorough reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author availability confirmed
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm that authors will be available to respond to media questions at and after release; list contact details.

rubrics_metrics.name: External expert contacts offered
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer contact information for independent experts to help reporters contextualize results and assess reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology document available
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make detailed methods documents available for reporters and experts to verify design, analysis, and reproducibility claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full paper PDF shared
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Share the full manuscript PDF when possible so reporters can read and verify claims rather than relying solely on the release.
